paper_title: The Role of Model Architecture and Scale in Predicting Molecular   Properties Insights from Fine-Tuning RoBERTa, BART, and LLaMA
caption: Training Loss vs. Steps for Each Model Type by Model Size with a Data Size of 20 millions. The loss trends for 10 million and 20 million datasets are similar.
model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the training loss over training steps for six different model configurations—ChemBART Small 20M, ChemBART Medium 20M, ChemBERTa Small 20M, ChemBERTa Medium 20M, ChemLLaMA Small 20M, and ChemLLaMA Medium 20M—each trained on a 20 million data point dataset. The x-axis, labeled “Step,” spans from 0K to 440K, with major tick marks at 0K, 20K, 40K, 60K, 80K, 420K, 430K, and 440K, indicating a non-uniform scale that zooms in on the final 20K steps. The y-axis, labeled “Train Loss,” ranges from 0.0 to 0.85 with tick marks at 0.0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.75, and 0.85. All six lines exhibit a steep initial decline in loss from approximately 0.85 at 0K steps to below 0.2 by 20K steps, followed by a slower, more gradual decrease toward convergence near 0.05–0.1 by 440K steps. The red line (ChemBART Small 20M) starts highest and remains slightly above others through most of training. The green line (ChemBERTa Small 20M) shows higher variance and occasional spikes, especially between 40K and 80K steps. The brown line (ChemLLaMA Medium 20M) and purple line (ChemLLaMA Small 20M) converge closely near the bottom, with the medium variant slightly lower in loss after 40K steps. The blue (ChemBART Medium 20M) and orange (ChemBERTa Medium 20M) lines track closely together, with the orange line slightly lower in loss after 20K steps. In the zoomed-in region from 420K to 440K, all lines flatten significantly, indicating convergence, with losses ranging between 0.05 and 0.08.
